transcript: to be honest it's getting a little bit difficult for me to engage with these Encores productions in like a critical way and part of it is that I think we've become a little bit hyper-fixated on the potential for Broadway transfers which like I get it because we've had more transfers recently and they've been doing more popular shows and the problem is that it's conditioned us or I'll speak for myself it's conditioned me to start thinking of these as like proper revivals instead of as the one-off special concert engagements that they were theoretically meant to be cause like I just have different standards for those two things and to be clear I'm not talking about set design I don't wanna get into set discourse I'll just get angry but like I don't really care if these shows have full sets for me it has much more to do with the short development and rehearsal time and like how much these artists can be expected to leave their stamp on the material and excavate everything there is to excavate in the text in that short amount of time so I end up judging them by standards that they were never really set up to meet and I think at least part of that is because we've been primed to think of them as potential Broadway revivals but then again there's also a case to be made for asking like: was this the right show for Encores if in fact the text is demanding that level of work? like if I know that all I have to reheat my leftovers is a microwave I'm gonna reheat the pasta and not the pizza because pasta does better in the microwave and I said this about the light in the piazza at encores on the dramatic side but now I would say the same thing about Urinetown on the comedic side because of course comedy is very difficult and it's not that this production wasn't funny it was but I was wanting them to have more time to really get into a rhythm find more of the characterizations find more of their own gags. the other part of this is that now that they're doing more of these popular fan favorite shows or cult favorite I know some people feel like it kind of betrayed the original mission of the encores series I don't feel that strongly about that element of it but one downside I do see is that if the audience is more familiar with the material if their memories of it are more recent or if they have access to it elsewhere that is another factor that's going to raise the standard like you're never gonna see a better production of Call Me Madam than the one at encores but you might have seen the original production of Urinetown and even if not you might have seen a fantastic regional or community theatre production like I saw a high school production that I thought was honestly more fun than this you'll notice that nothing I've said in this video is really the fault of the artists it's all due to circumstances outside of their control which is why I started this video by saying
